item.title: Landman' star Ali Larter shows off her fit physique in barely-there bikinis during yacht vacation in Italy
item.description: Ali Larter, 50, shared stunning bikini photos from her Italian superyacht vacation, showcasing the fitness routine that keeps her camera-ready.
item.content:encoded:
Ali Larter flaunted her fit physique in several skimpy bikinis while soaking up the sun during a vacation in Italy.

On Saturday, the 50-year-old actress shared a carousel of photos featuring moments from her getaway on a superyacht in the Italian Rivera.

In one snap, the "Landman" star rocked a nude-toned metallic bikini as she sunbathed on a red and white lounge chair while out at sea.

'LANDMAN' STAR ALI LARTER ESCAPED TO IDAHO AFTER HOLLYWOOD'S 'MANY' SOCIAL DEMANDS

Larter's two-piece featured a ruched bandeau top with a circle keyhole cutout and bottoms that had gold chain detailing on the sides. She accessorized with black oval sunglasses and several gold rings.

The "Varsity Blues" actress draped one arm over the cushion behind her head as she beamed at the camera.

In a selfie, Larter donned a black bandeau bikini top accented with gold hardware and black ruffled shorts while cozying up to her husband Hayes MacArthur as they posed at the side of the yacht against a backdrop of the rocky coastline and ocean.

Larter wore a lingerie-style white lace halter top bikini with nude lining in another photo that she shared. She wore the two-piece under a sheer aquamarine blue cover-up that was embellished with white and turquoise stones that lined Larter's neckline and chest.

In the image, Larter posed for the camera as she descended wooden steps on the yacht under a blue sky dotted with white clouds.

The "Final Destination" star also showed off more of her summer style, sporting a plunging light blue and white printed minidress while standing in front of a bar and flashing a bright smile. She was also pictured in a brightly-colored flowing cover-up as she strolled on the deck of the yacht.

'LANDMAN' STAR MICHELLE RANDOLPH STUNS IN BARELY-THERE METALLIC YELLOW BIKINI IN NEW SUMMER PHOTO DUMP

Larter, who is known for her dedication to fitness, was seen in a black Alo sports bra with matching leggings during a workout session in a gym on the yacht.

In her carousel, Larter included other photos featuring a plate of pasta with a glass of wine, a sunset and a selfie in which she was seen wearing a red top with a diamond necklace and a headset. Later concluded her slideshow with a loved-up snap of herself with MacArthur that was taken on the yacht at night.

"🇮🇹 Adoro l’Italia 🇮🇹," she wrote in the caption of her post.

While Larter has occasionally shared swimsuit photos on her Instagram page, the actress previously admitted her bikini scenes in "Landman" are the most challenging for her to film.

SHAKIRA SOAKS UP THE MIAMI SUN AS BIKINI-CLAD NINA DOBREV, KIM KARDASHIAN SHOWCASE SUMMER GETAWAYS

During a January interview with People magazine, the 49-year-old actress, who plays Angela Norris in the hit Paramount+ series, described shooting scenes in which her character wears a bikini as "tough, in a weird way."

"I don't think there's an actress alive that's like, 'Woo! Got a bikini scene!' " Larter said. "Nobody wants to do it.

"Those are the hardest for me," she continued. "I don't enjoy them. It's just part of the story that I'm telling, and I'm an actress, so I get on board. But those are definitely my least favorite."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Angela is the confident and glamorous ex-wife of Billy Bob Thornton's Tommy Norris. The "Varsity Blues" star noted that her character is "so physical and loves the spray tans, and the blonde."

Larter explained that portraying Angela, who is often clad in revealing clothing, requires effort and discipline to ensure that she is "staying in shape for this role and all that comes with it."

While speaking with People in November, Larter shared how she adheres to a strict diet and fitness routine while filming the show.

HILARIA BALDWIN FLAUNTS FIT FIGURE IN BIKINI AS FANS MARVEL AT MOM OF 7

"I'll tell you what. I work really hard, OK? I'm not pretending that I don't," she said. "I'm up at 4:30 [a.m.] on Mondays. I go for a run. It's only 30 minutes. I try to eat very clean, but I eat. I'm one of those protein mommies. I eat so much protein all day long. It works for me."

She explained that, in addition to running, she also does "a lot of strength training."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"In the end, anytime you have to put on a bathing suit and walk in front of anybody, it's really difficult," she said. "When I look around, the sexiest women I know are the women that own it. So, part of getting there with Angela is owning it."

"But no matter what, it's like, I've got to spend all this time fighting off my own insecurities, my own anxiety, to be able to put on that bikini and walk into these scenes," she admitted.

Larter told People that "there is no space in my mind for insecurity" when playing Angela.

"I wouldn't be able to do it if I allowed insecurity to creep in," she said. "And I really do believe, sexiness — yeah, she's sexy on the outside, but guess what? She's owning it on the inside, too."

"Landman" is expected to premiere its third season in early 2027 with production slated to begin in late August or early September.

item.title: President Trump celebrates Bedminster club championship, brags little practice was needed to score a 70
item.description: Trump posted a scorecard of 70 at Bedminster's championship course, claiming his 40th club championship title in the senior division on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
It's a tough Sunday for the "Trump can't ..." crowd. For months, the mainstream media pounced on President Donald J. Trump, claiming he was physically washed up and incapable of even swinging a golf club.

But on Sunday, No. 47 walked onto one of the toughest championship courses in the country, fired a 70, took the Senior Division title, and captured what he said was his 40th club championship title.

LIBERALS MELT DOWN AFTER LEARNING PGA TOUR IS RETURNING TO TRUMP-OWNED GOLF COURSE

A reported 2-under round on a championship course is the sort of result that stands out regardless of who posts it. If you thought the Commander-in-Chief would walk away humbly, you don't know the guy.

Posting on Truth Social after the victory, President Trump said: "The Winning Shot in the Bedminster Club Championship! Thank you very much to all of those who participated. I won with a score of 70, and am so honored in that, unlike the rest of the field, I'm given very little time to practice, because I'm focused on many other things. It's called TALENT, and I have it, and they don't! President DONALD J. TRUMP"

DR MARC SIEGEL: WHAT DR OZ SAYS ABOUT TRUMP’S DIET MAY SURPRISE HIS HARSHEST CRITICS

Let's put this into proper perspective because a 70 at Trump National Golf Club in Bedminster is not an average go.

Based on the score he reported, Trump finished 2-under par to claim the Senior crown.

In NFL terms, it's like watching Joe Namath throw a 40-yard touchdown pass in 2026.

A 70 at Trump National Golf Club in Bedminster, New Jersey, is spectacular given the club's Tom Fazio-designed championship courses have hosted the U.S. Women's Open and LIV Golf events, and are packed with water hazards and deep bunkers.

The blue-check media spent months questioning Trump's stamina in ways they never did Joe Biden, insisting he couldn't navigate 18 holes.

The same critics who swore he couldn't physically play are going to lose their collective minds over this scorecard. They'll assign investigative journalists to measure divots, demand official audits from club pros, or whine about gimme putts.

Meanwhile, Trump walks away with trophy number 40, leaving the media to do what they do best: cope.

item.title: Spencer Pratt reacts to Spokane devastation with blunt wildfire warning and message of faith
item.description: Spencer Pratt urges families not to wait for disaster after Spokane wildfire evacuation displaces thousands, drawing on his Palisades Fire experience.
item.content:encoded:
As crews battle fast-moving wildfires that have destroyed hundreds of structures and forced thousands to evacuate in the Spokane area, one wildfire survivor is urging Americans to prepare before disaster strikes.

Former Los Angeles mayoral candidate and reality personality Spencer Pratt, whose Pacific Palisades home was destroyed in the 2025 Palisades Fire, said the devastation unfolding in Spokane is a warning for communities across the country.

"My deepest sympathies to the folks in Spokane who just lost everything in an instant," Pratt wrote in a lengthy social media post Sunday. "Nothing can really prepare you for this devastation."

Pratt, who has been outspoken about the emotional and financial toll of losing his own home, warned that communities across the country should not assume they are immune from similar disasters.

PALISADES FIRE SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY DRIVEN BY 'SOCIETAL REVENGE,' BEHAVIORAL ANALYST TESTIFIES IN COURT

"And everyone else, take heed... this is coming for you, too," he wrote. "Don't wait til the fire is at your patio door."

He urged families to have an evacuation plan in place before disaster strikes, cautioning that wildfires often spread too quickly to leave time for last-minute decisions.

WOULD THIS SURVIVAL POD MAKE YOU FEEL SAFER?

"Have a plan. Don't expect government to be there to save your home," Pratt wrote. "Don't expect the fire to wait until you're at home and awake and ready... think about what happens when the fire comes at 2AM dead asleep, or when you're at work downtown, or 3 beers in on a river float 20 miles from home and your cats are all locked inside. You seldom get a real warning before the fire comes."

Pratt also reflected on the heartbreaking losses families face beyond their homes.

"As of now, I've not seen any reports of fatalities, thank God, and I pray there were none, but a lot of beloved pets undoubtedly perished, and for many, that's like losing family," he wrote.

EXCLUSIVE: WOMAN WHO STOLE $1.7M MEANT FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS GETS PRISON TIME AS DHS CRACKS DOWN ON FEMA FRAUD

He encouraged neighbors to support one another through what he predicted would be a lengthy recovery.

"Please look after your neighbors; they have a very long and painful road ahead, and everyone will move on from caring about Spokane in a week or so," Pratt wrote.

Pratt concluded his message by encouraging those affected to lean on their faith.

"Above all else, if I can offer any advice right now... lean further into God," he wrote. "The Lord is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit. Have faith in His providence, even if your heart feels too broken to accept it right now."

Amid the devastation, former Washington state Rep. Matt Shea shared a photo of an American flag still standing after flames swept through a neighborhood, calling it "an amazing picture of hope among the ashes."

"Some friends of ours lost everything... but Old Glory still survives," Shea wrote on X. "What an amazing picture of hope among the ashes. Thank you all for praying for us."

Former Seattle Seahawks quarterback Russell Wilson also shared a message of support on X, writing, "Praying for Spokane!"

As messages of support poured in, firefighters continued battling three major blazes being managed as part of the Spokane-area wildfire response.

According to Incident Commander Benjamin Cossel with the U.S. Department of Agriculture, the Autumn Lane Fire has burned 3,333 acres, the Old Trail Fire has scorched 3,481 acres, and the Fairview Fire has grown to 914 acres. All three fires remained 0% contained as of the latest update.

More than 900 firefighters and support personnel have been deployed across the three fires, with the Autumn Lane Fire remaining the primary focus.

Authorities said approximately 5,000 homes have been evacuated as firefighters continue battling the blazes. Incident command has confirmed more than 600 structures have been destroyed, though officials cautioned that number could rise as crews gain access to damaged areas.

The American Red Cross Northwest Region said more than 400 people and their pets spent Saturday night at an emergency shelter in Spokane after the fast-moving wildfires forced widespread evacuations.

"Extreme weather conditions led three separate wildfires to wreak havoc on Saturday, forcing widespread evacuations, causing extensive destruction, and forever changing the lives of those affected," the Red Cross said, adding that it has launched a "massive relief effort" and is seeking donations and volunteers to assist displaced residents.

Rep. Michael Baumgartner, R-Wash., said he spoke with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin about the fire situation and potential federal assistance.

"After Gov. Ferguson requests emergency assistance he will take the official request for FEMA support to President Trump," Baumgartner wrote on X, adding that he appreciated Mullin's "care and concern for what our community is experiencing."

Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson later said he spoke directly with President Donald Trump and Mullin, describing the devastation unfolding in Spokane and elsewhere across the state.

"Just a few minutes ago, I spoke with President Trump and Secretary Mullin. I detailed how dire and devastating the situation is in Spokane and across our state," Ferguson wrote on X.

Ferguson said Trump "expressed his concern for the people of Washington during this difficult time" and that the two would "be working together on additional requests for federal assistance."

"I deeply appreciate the President taking time to have this conversation, and I am optimistic we will receive a quick approval for our request for a federal emergency declaration," Ferguson wrote.

Sen. Patty Murray, D-Wash., said she also spoke with Mullin and said the federal government is closely tracking the disaster.

"He made clear the federal government will do everything it can to support response and recovery—that is my top priority right now and I deeply appreciate that commitment," Murray wrote on X.

Calling the destruction "heartbreaking," Murray said "it will be a long road to recovery."

"Right now, EVERYONE needs to listen carefully to local officials," she wrote. "I am so grateful to our fire crews and first responders who are saving lives, including our WA National Guard, servicemembers from Fairchild, and the many individuals coming from out of state to fight these fires."

As the response continued, the Spokane County Board of Commissioners unanimously declared a state of emergency, giving county officials additional authority to quickly purchase emergency equipment and supplies.

"My heart goes out to those who have been affected by these devastating fires and my prayers are with the first responders who will continue working through the night and into tomorrow," Spokane County Commissioner Mary Brooks said.

Officials also urged people to stay away from lakes, rivers and other waterways where firefighting aircraft are collecting water to battle the blazes.

Emergency officials warned boaters, kayakers, paddleboarders and others on the water to give aircraft plenty of space as they make frequent low-level passes, saying doing so is critical to keeping both crews and the public safe while allowing firefighters to continue protecting threatened communities.

Fox News' Sarah Alegre contributed to this report.

item.title: James Carville vows to abandon Democratic Party if far-left Hasan Piker becomes leading voice
item.description: James Carville vows to leave the Democratic Party if socialist streamer Hasan Piker becomes a leading force, warning the two-party system faces stress.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic strategist James Carville pledged to leave the Democratic Party if far-left streamer Hasan Piker becomes a leading voice in it and argued that an "overwhelming majority" of Democrats agree.

"I am not going to be in the same party with Hasan Piker," he said on "The Sunday Briefing." 

"If he becomes a force in a Democratic Party, I'm out of here. I have no intention of ever being in the same political party with that guy," Carville continued. 

Piker, a self-described socialist streamer who campaigned with Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, has emerged as a leading voice on the left as democratic socialists gain ground in elections across the country.

WISCONSIN DEMOCRAT DOWNPLAYS APPEARING ON HASAN PIKER'S SHOW, DOESN'T 'ENDORSE' EVERYTHING HE SAYS

Piker drew widespread criticism after saying "America deserved 9/11" during a stream in 2019. He later said in an interview that he "obviously" did not mean America deserved the attacks and defended the viral quote as a critique of U.S. foreign policy.

"I can't sit here and tell you for certain how this is going to turn out, but the one thing I can tell you for certain, Hasan Piker and James Carville are not going to be in the same political party. One of us is going to leave. It might even be me," Carville told Fox News.

Piker recently named Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., as his preferred Democratic presidential candidate for 2028 and argued there is "0% chance" the Democratic nominee will be pro-Israel in "any way, shape or form" as polling shows support for Israel has collapsed among Democrats.

CASH-STRAPPED DNC SHELLED OUT MORE THAN $800K TO NON-VOTING TERRITORIES LIKE VIRGIN ISLANDS WHILE IN DEBT

The rise of democratic socialism comes as the Democratic National Committee (DNC) faces internal challenges, with Chair Ken Martin grappling with mounting debt. Carville said the DNC will have to "un-constipate itself," adding that he "can’t help them."

With several DSA-endorsed candidates winning their respective primaries across the nation, socialism’s growing influence has intensified debate within the Democratic Party over its ideological direction. 

"It may be that the two-party system is just going to be under tremendous stress here in the coming months," Carville said.

Carville has raised concerns over far-left candidates, saying in a recent CNN interview that many of them are "too hard-headed to know that they’re not popular," adding that "people don’t like them."

Carville also warned that democratic socialists are dragging the party’s brand "through the mud."

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Early eating habits could have lasting effects on dementia risk, study suggests
item.description: A study of about 64,000 people found that lower sugar intake during pregnancy and early life was linked to up to 23% lower dementia risk decades later.
item.content:encoded:
Consuming less sugar during pregnancy and the first years of life may lower the risk of developing dementia decades later, according to new research.

A study published in Neurology found that people who were exposed to less sugar before birth and during their first one to two years of life had up to a 23% lower risk of developing dementia compared with those born after sugar became widely available again.

Researchers examined the health records of more than 64,000 people in the United Kingdom who were born before and after World War II sugar rationing ended in 1953.

People who experienced lower sugar intake before birth and through their first year of life had a 21% lower risk of dementia, while those whose sugar intake remained limited through age two had a 23% lower risk, researchers found.

DAILY EATING HABIT LINKED TO BETTER BRAIN HEALTH IN OLDER ADULTS, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

The study also found that people with lower sugar exposure early in life developed dementia an average of 2.6 years later than those who consumed more sugar.

"Our findings suggest that limiting sugar during the earliest stages of life may have lasting benefits for brain health," study author Jiazhen Zheng of The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology said in the press release.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Dariush Mozaffarian, director of the Food is Medicine Institute at Tufts University, who was not involved in the study, said the research raises an interesting question but cautioned against drawing firm conclusions.

"I'm impressed with the researchers' creativity, pulling together information across decades to look at this question, but the findings are not convincing," Mozaffarian told Fox News Digital.

He said many other factors likely differed between people born during and after wartime, including overall nutrition and calorie intake, making it difficult to know whether sugar alone explains the difference.

Still, Mozaffarian said the broader guidance for pregnant women remains the same.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"Ultimately, we know from other research that women who are pregnant should consume the healthiest foods possible for both their own health and that of their baby," he told Fox News Digital.

He recommended focusing on minimally processed foods such as fruits, vegetables, beans, nuts, seeds, whole grains, fermented dairy products and fish while limiting ultra-processed foods high in sugar, starch and salt.

Researchers stressed that the study found only an association between early-life sugar intake and dementia risk and does not prove that reducing sugar directly prevents the disease.

Researchers also noted several limitations, including that the study used exposure to a historical rationing policy as a proxy for individual sugar intake and could not eliminate the influence of other differences between the groups.

As a result, the findings cannot establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship between lower sugar intake early in life and a reduced risk of dementia.

item.title: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has Tony Romo's back, believes he will 'work through' OWI arrest
item.description: Jerry Jones said Tony Romo will "work through" his recent Wisconsin OWI arrest, praising his former quarterback's ability to handle adversity.
item.content:encoded:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones believes his former franchise quarterback, Tony Romo, will "work through" his recent OWI arrest in Wisconsin.

Jones, who saw Romo under center for 13 seasons in Dallas, talked about him during a recent interview with KDFW Fox 4, saying he has been in contact with the quarterback-turned-broadcaster.

Romo was arrested on July 23 on charges of operating a vehicle while under the influence, as well as allegedly possessing an open container of alcohol in his vehicle and unsafe passing to the right.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I love him," Jones said. "I love what he’s about. I love his character. I love his love of sport. And he’s a very, very unique talent. And the real question is – and I don’t even have to ask what the answer is: Do you think Tony Romo knows how to get up when he gets knocked down? He had a life of that. And absolutely, that’s one of his greatest attributes, is that he can handle adversity.

"So this is something that he will work though. He is a unique talent.… So, obviously, I’m a big fan of his, big fan of his family, and let me tell you right now, he’s as real as he sounds. He feels every down time, he feels every up time."

TONY ROMO ARRESTED IN MILWAUKEE FOR ALLEGED OWI OFFENSE: REPORT

Romo’s case has been quite the NFL storyline as training camp began across the league last week, especially as police bodycam footage became available.

Romo, who was driving after playing a round in the Wisconsin Amateur Golf Championship, was seen telling police that he had "zero" drinks, and even questioned why they thought he was intoxicated.

"Because I’m coming from a golf course, you think I’m drunk?" Romo was heard saying.

Romo was detained by police and transported to a nearby station to conduct field sobriety tests after the arresting officer said she observed red, glassy eyes and smelled alcohol on Romo’s breath.

After completing the tests, Romo refused to take a breath test, telling the officer, "I've heard from all the lawyers don't ever do that."

NFL ANALYST TONY ROMO PLACED ON LEAVE BY CBS SPORTS FOLLOWING DRUNK DRIVING ARREST IN WISCONSIN

A week later, Romo was sidelined by CBS Sports as their top NFL analyst alongside play-by-play voice Jim Nantz. The network announced this past Friday that Romo "is on leave from his role at CBS Sports until further notice."

It is unclear how this leave will be observed for Romo, but former Houston Texans great defensive end J.J. Watt will be taking his place in the booth next to Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson.

The 46-year-old became CBS’ top NFL analyst on April 4, 2017, which was the same day he announced his retirement from the NFL.

Romo threw for 34,183 yards, 248 touchdowns and 117 interceptions, completing 65.3% of his passes during his career.

item.title: Off-duty trooper and armed citizen hailed as heroes after returning fire on In-N-Out gunman
item.description: Police identified Chad Williams as the suspect in the Twin Falls, Idaho, In-N-Out Burger shooting that left three people dead and seven others injured.
item.content:encoded:
Police identified the man accused of opening fire Saturday at a recently opened In-N-Out Burger location in Twin Falls, Idaho, revealing he was subdued by an off-duty state trooper and an armed citizen who returned fire during the shooting.

The suspected gunman, identified as Chad Williams, 24, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound after fatally shooting an employee and a customer, according to Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks.

Authorities believe Williams acted alone in the attack. He was found dead near the restaurant.

IN-N-OUT PRESIDENT SAYS ‘HEART IS BROKEN’ AFTER EMPLOYEE, CUSTOMERS KILLED IN IDAHO SHOOTING

"We want to take a moment and commend the actions of the off-duty officer and the citizen and their heroic action to stop this incident," Hicks said during a news conference Sunday. "We believe their actions helped drive the suspect away from the scene, preventing further casualties."

Three people died, and seven others were wounded in the shootout, city spokesperson Josh Palmer previously said.

Authorities said two of the injured victims have been released from the hospital, while three are in stable condition and two remain in critical condition.

MULTIPLE PEOPLE KILLED IN SHOOTING AT IDAHO IN-N-OUT RESTAURANT, SUSPECT DEAD

Hicks described the incident as one of the most "chaotic" situations his department has faced, saying first responders encountered a scenario unlike anything many law enforcement officers experience in their careers.

The investigation has expanded to include multiple agencies, including local law enforcement partners and the FBI.

FBI Salt Lake City Special Agent in Charge Robert Boles said the bureau has committed its full resources to the investigation.

"We have committed the full weight of our resources to the Twin Falls Police Department, deploying every investigative and intelligence tool at our disposal," Boles said. "Our evidence response teams and victim services specialists are also on the ground, working tirelessly to support both the investigation and those impacted."

Officials said officers from the Meridian, Caldwell and Nampa police departments were sworn in to assist the Idaho State Police with patrols in Twin Falls.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Chris Sabin, Alex Shelley make All Elite Wrestling debut
item.description: The Motor City Machine Guns debuted on AEW "Collision" in Detroit, aligning with the Bang Bang Gang after an eight-man tag team match turned chaotic.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Sabin and Alex Shelley made their All Elite Wrestling (AEW) debuts on "Collision" earlier this week as the show took place in the tag team’s hometown of Detroit.

Sabin and Shelley, collectively known as the Motor City Machine Guns, put the AEW tag team on notice and said they were with the company because it was where the best wrestle.

"Did you really think we wouldn’t be here? There’s no place we’d rather be in than the greatest city in civilization," Sabin said. "The place we represented for 20 years. Because this is where the best wrestle."

The Motor City Machine Guns didn’t take long to make an impact.

item.title: Will Levis supremely confident he is capable of being NFL starter while battling for Titans' backup role
item.description: Will Levis claims there aren't 32 quarterbacks better than him despite facing a QB3 role behind Cam Ward and Mitchell Trubisky in Nashville.
item.content:encoded:
Tennessee Titans quarterback Will Levis hasn't played a competitive snap of football since January 2025. Despite that fact, with questions about his health and the situation he currently finds himself in Nashville, the signal-caller has not lost one ounce of confidence.

Levis will likely find himself as the third-string quarterback for the Titans to begin the year, with former first-overall pick Cam Ward entering year two as QB1, but certainly isn't shying away from the tremendous challenge ahead of him of becoming a starting quarterback in the NFL again.

"There are not 32 quarterbacks in this league better than me. I know that for sure," Levis, who has made 21 starts for the Titans, told reporters in Music City on Saturday. "I know I’ve put the tape out there already that I’m a dang good quarterback in this league."

TITANS' WILL LEVIS FACED SEX TAPE HACK, SPENT 'EXORBITANT AMOUNT OF MONEY' TO INVESTIGATE, MOM SAYS

"I’m not worried about the competition per se or the amount of opportunities that they’re going to give me," he continued. "I just got to make sure that I’m ready for when they are given to me and just preparing to be the best at that as possible."

Levis isn't wrong in saying he has tape as an NFL starting quarterback, but his claim that it is "dang good" would be debated by most.

The former Kentucky star owns a 5-16 record as a starter while throwing for 21 touchdowns and 16 interceptions to go along with a whopping 17 fumbles.

While the Titans' roster around him did him no favors during his time as the starting quarterback, Levis didn't exactly light the world on fire in the early stages of his career.

The 27-year-old underwent season-ending surgery on his throwing shoulder in July 2025 and spent the year on the injured reserve list for Tennessee. Levis, who is set to become a free agent at the end of the 2026 NFL season, is battling against veteran Mitchell Trubisky for the backup role with the season fast approaching.

There is nothing wrong with Levis believing that he is a Top 32 quarterback in the NFL, but stating it while staring at the QB3 position on the depth chart in the early stages of training camp is overzealous.

item.title: Bernie Sanders blasts Fetterman as 'way out of touch' with Americans after Graham Platner rebuke
item.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders fired back at Sen. John Fetterman on "Meet the Press," citing a Quinnipiac poll showing just 19% approval for Fetterman among Pennsylvania Democrats.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., criticized Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., as "way out of touch" with Americans on Sunday after Fetterman recently accused him of showing no regret over endorsing scandal-plagued former Maine Senate nominee Graham Platner.

Sanders responded by citing Fetterman’s standing among Pennsylvania Democrats, arguing that the senator was disconnected from voters on Israel and other issues.

"Well, my response to Fetterman is last time I saw it, he was reflecting the views of about 19% of the Democrats in the state of Pennsylvania," Sanders said on "Meet the Press."

"I think probably lower than any other member of the Democratic Senate. Fetterman does his thing, and I think, on Israel, and many other issues, is way out of touch with the people of America," Sanders said.

SEN JOHN FETTERMAN PLEDGES TO BE 'LAST MAN STANDING' IN THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY IN SUPPORT OF ISRAEL

Sanders appeared to be referencing a July Quinnipiac University survey that found 19% of Pennsylvania Democrats approved of Fetterman's job performance, while 69% disapproved. The same survey found that 77% of Republicans approved of Fetterman, although his overall approval rating among registered voters was 48%.

When reached for comment on Sanders' Sunday commentary, Fetterman’s office pointed Fox News Digital to remarks he shared with Semafor on Thursday in which he intensified his criticism of Sanders over the collapse of Platner’s campaign. The Pennsylvania Democrat accused Sanders of promoting Platner amid multiple controversies and scandals before the former candidate withdrew from Maine’s Senate race.

"You were the carnival barker for an accused rapist. You should have taken my advice, since you and P-Hustle blew up the Maine race," Fetterman said. "Take responsibility and apologize."

FETTERMAN BRANDS NEW SOCIALIST FAVORITE 'PONTIAC PLATNER' AFTER 'OGRE' DIG

"After you just blasted the Maine race apart, you are in Michigan replicating it," Fetterman said, referring to Sanders' support of progressive Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

The clash followed months of tension between the senators over Platner and the Democratic Party's approach to Israel. 

"Meet the Press" host Kristen Welker played a clip in which Fetterman accused Sanders of helping elevate Platner despite controversies surrounding the former candidate.

"I would be frustrated with someone like Bernie Sanders," Fetterman said. "You know, why, why aren’t people angry why they promoted, you know, someone like Platner, an accused rapist."

"So really, Bernie, you have no regret endorsing and proud to stand with an accused rapist, a guy that roughs-up his ex-girlfriends, a guy that had a Nazi tattoo on his chest."

JOHN FETTERMAN ERUPTS OVER 'CREEPER' GRAHAM PLATNER, SUGGESTING HE'S A 'NAZI SYMPATHIZER'

Fetterman previously demanded that Sanders apologize to Maine voters and everyone who donated to Platner's campaign. 

Sanders later called for Platner to leave the race after a former girlfriend accused him of rape, an allegation Platner denied.

Welker asked Sanders whether he regretted endorsing Platner before the allegation emerged. Sanders defended the campaign Platner ran, while acknowledging the seriousness of the accusation that prompted his withdrawal.

"Well, you know, it’s easy to be a Monday morning quarterback," Sanders said. "Platner ran a very strong campaign and, in fact, many of the issues that he’s raised are resonating all over this country. A woman made very serious allegations against him, he withdrew from the race, period."

item.title: Caitlin Clark, Fever finally run out of gas against Lynx after brutal WNBA travel schedule
item.description: Kelsey Mitchell scored 37 points and Caitlin Clark posted a double-double, but Indiana's grueling schedule caught up in a 108-100 loss to Minnesota.
item.content:encoded:
The Indiana Fever finally ran out of gas Sunday afternoon.

It just took the best team in the WNBA, playing at home, to make it happen.

TRANS ACTIVISTS HARASS, HURL SLURS AT SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS BEFORE FEVER GAME IN MINNESOTA

The Minnesota Lynx defeated Indiana, 108-100, snapping the Fever’s five-game winning streak and improving to a league-best 25-6. Minnesota extended its own winning streak to 10 straight, while Indiana fell to 19-11.

The Lynx were clearly the better team on Sunday at the Target Center and made several huge plays when Indiana threatened to complete a furious fourth-quarter comeback.

But the WNBA certainly didn’t do the Fever any favors.

Indiana was playing its third road game in six days, with stops in Seattle, Portland and Minneapolis, and this one started roughly 36 hours after Friday’s late game in Portland.

Despite that, the Fever showed plenty of fight.

Minnesota appeared to put the game away when Courtney Williams’ jumper gave the Lynx a 98-84 lead with 5:39 remaining.

CHERYL REEVE SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM OVER "TRANS KIDS BELONG" SHIRT AT FEVER-LYNX GAME

Indiana responded with a 14-2 run to pull within 100-98, forcing Minnesota to execute under pressure after seemingly having the game wrapped up.

Olivia Miles slowed the comeback, and Courtney Williams helped close it out.

Miles converted an and-one with 58 seconds remaining, pushing Minnesota’s lead back to 105-98 and effectively sealing the victory. The three-point play gave Miles 28 points on a ridiculous 11-of-14 shooting.

Williams added a clutch basket with 32 seconds left to put the game out of reach. She finished with 27 points on 12-of-20 shooting, meaning the two Minnesota guards combined for 55 points.

Indiana’s Big Three drove the action on the other end.

Kelsey Mitchell served as the scoring engine, pouring in 37 points on 14-of-21 shooting. She connected on six of her eight three-point attempts.

Caitlin Clark controlled the offense as a facilitator, finishing with 19 points and 10 assists for her eighth double-double this season. Aliyah Boston contributed across the board with 15 points, seven rebounds and seven assists.

Together, Mitchell, Clark and Boston accounted for 71 of Indiana’s 100 points and 20 of its 27 assists.

The Fever shot 57% from the field and scored at least 100 points for the sixth consecutive game, extending the longest such streak in WNBA history.

Indiana’s offense wasn't the problem, but the team looked tired on the defensive end at times. Looking at their recent schedule, it's not hard to see why.

Indiana played Friday night in Portland in a game that didn’t begin until 10 p.m. ET. It ended after midnight on the East Coast.

The Fever then had Saturday to travel two time zones east before Sunday’s 1 p.m. ET tipoff in Minnesota.

That left roughly 36 hours between the final buzzer in Portland and the opening tip against the Lynx, with a travel day in between.

Technically, it wasn’t a back-to-back.

In practical terms, it wasn’t much better.

And the Portland-to-Minnesota turnaround was only the final portion of a demanding stretch for Indiana’s best players.

Clark, Mitchell and Boston all participated in the WNBA All-Star Game in Chicago last Saturday. The Fever then traveled across the country to play Seattle on Tuesday, remained in the Pacific Northwest for Friday’s game in Portland and flew east to Minnesota for Sunday’s matchup.

That’s an All-Star break followed by three road games in three different cities over nine days.

Some "break."

Clark raised concerns about the schedule immediately after the All-Star Game.

"It’s a tough turnaround, and the Fever probably have one of the quickest turnarounds," Clark said. "We played on Wednesday, and I’m going home tonight and I’m flying to Seattle tomorrow."

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FANS ALLEGE STORM PLAYERS, EXEC HECKLED GIRLS DURING GAME OVER SUPPORT OF WOMEN'S SPORTS

She wasn’t alone.

Several All-Star players questioned the lack of recovery time, including New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart.

"If you want it to be competitive, then there needs to be more time," Stewart said while discussing the All-Star Game. "I can’t play on Wednesday, and then I have a game on Tuesday, and you want me to go balls to the walls on Saturday."

The Fever’s subsequent schedule illustrated the larger problem.

ESPN reported during the broadcast that Clark had been "getting sick" before Sunday’s game.

The Fever didn't immediately provide additional information, and there’s no way to know whether it had anything to do with exhaustion, travel or an unrelated illness.

Still, Clark clearly wasn’t entering the game under ideal circumstances.

That made the league’s scheduling decision especially puzzling.

This wasn’t an ordinary regular-season matchup. It was a marquee Sunday afternoon national television game on ABC featuring the WNBA’s best team against its most popular team in an important weekend sports time slot.

The WNBA had every reason to want both teams, and especially its biggest stars, at their best.

Instead, it sent Indiana into the showcase less than two days after a late game on the other side of the country.

The good news for the Fever is that the gauntlet is finally over.

Indiana is going home and doesn’t play again until Thursday against the Las Vegas Aces, giving the team three full days without a game after a stretch that sent its All-Stars from Chicago to Seattle, Portland and Minnesota.

The Fever earned the rest.

The WNBA should have given them more of it before Sunday.

item.title: Los Angeles Dodgers trade for Tarik Skubal higlights Major League Baseball's massive problem
item.description: The Tarik Skubal trade to the Los Angeles Dodgers exposes MLB's real problem: most owners prioritize surplus value over winning a World Series.
item.content:encoded:
Late Saturday night, the Los Angeles Dodgers did the expected, and the unthinkable, and traded for superstar starter and the reigning American League Cy Young Award winner, Tarik Skubal.

The Dodgers sent a trio of young players to the Detroit Tigers, outfielder Zyhir Hope, pitcher River Ryan, and another minor league pitcher, Brady Smith. Hope ranked 26th overall in The Athletic’s latest prospect update, and Ryan ranked 41st. Smith was described by Fangraphs as having "nasty stuff," and as of last week, was striking out over 14 hitters per nine innings in the minor leagues.

To say the trade sent shockwaves through baseball fan social media would be a massive understatement. Outrage reigned supreme, with many bewildered "that’s all the Tigers got?" Along with the usual, "cancel the season," "cancel next season," "we want a lockout," and many other irrational seething diatribes.

DODGERS REPORTEDLY ACQUIRE ACE TARIK SKUBAL FROM TIGERS IN TRADE THAT STIRS UP MLB WORLD

But while the trade, like all deadline deals, is sure to have its critics and defenders, one thing about it is certain: Major League Baseball has a problem. It’s just not the one that the anti-Dodgers, cancel the season, lockout brigade thinks it is.

First, it’s important to define what this trade is, and isn’t, because many casual fans don’t seem to fully understand how it works. Yes, the Dodgers traded for Tarik Skubal. But for many, that implies he’ll spend the rest of his career in Los Angeles. That may or may not be the case, but that’s not what this trade determines.

Modern front offices, and dedicated fans, understand that for a player whose contract expires at the end of the season, any trade is not for the rest of their career, it’s for the remaining 9-10 regular season starts. That’s it. The Dodgers are overwhelming favorites to make the postseason, but should the unlikely happen and say, they lose 20 games in a row and miss out, they’ll have traded those players just for Skubal’s regular season starts. The return the Tigers got for 9-10 starts was outstanding, by that measure.

Hope has yet to reach the major leagues, meaning he has six seasons of team control ahead of him. He’s just 21-years-old, but dominating AA to the tune of 23 home runs and 18 steals in just 94 games. Overall, he’s hitting .293/.369/.530. Obviously that doesn’t mean he’ll replicate those statistics in the big leagues immediately, but the Tigers now have him in their organization for six major league seasons at well below market rates.

Ryan has started his major league service time clock, but prospect evaluators believe he’s ready to pitch in a rotation right now, with a "monster" fastball, per Fangraphs. He struck out nearly 11 hitters per nine innings in the minors, while walking less than two. Some bad luck on batted balls in play makes his ERA look worse, but his underlying metrics are impressive. He’s under control for years to come. Incredibly, in yet another testament to the Dodgers' front office, they acquired Zyhir Hope in a trade with the Cubs, and River Ryan from the Padres for a utility player who's now out of baseball.

Still, all this for maybe nine starts, and a five-day exclusive negotiating window, for a player represented by Scott Boras. Boras clients are well known for rarely, if ever, signing extensions, instead waiting for the open market to identify the highest bidder.

There’s an assumption the Dodgers will automatically sign Skubal to a long-term contract because of the trade. They may well try, but unless it comes in that five-day window, the trade will have nothing to do with it. The Dodgers traded for Manny Machado in 2018 and let him leave for the San Diego Padres. They traded for Max Scherzer and Trea Turner in 2021. Both left in free agency when their contracts expired. They traded for Yu Darvish in 2017, and he too left in free agency. Corey Seager, a homegrown Dodgers star, signed with the Texas Rangers after the 2021 season.

Given Boras’ track record, it’s a near-certainty the other 29 teams will have the same ability, if they so choose, to sign Skubal. Which is where the problem with this trade, and the reaction to it, starts. The Dodgers didn’t trade for Skubal because they outspend everyone. Any team in baseball could afford to take on the remainder of his salary. They got Skubal because, and this is where MLB’s big issue lies, they are one of a handful of teams that actually cares about winning.

Yes, the Dodgers gave up two very high quality prospects for Skubal. But teams like the Brewers, Rays, Braves or Cubs, may have been able to top LA’s offer. They weren’t willing to. Not because they don’t have quality prospects of their own, or because they couldn’t afford to pay his salary, but because they don’t seem to understand what should be the primary goal in competitive sports: winning is. Flags fly forever. Championship banners last forever.

You know what doesn’t last forever? Surplus prospect value.

Milwaukee has been the best team in baseball the last two years. They have a better record than Los Angeles thus far in 2026, and they finished four games ahead of the Dodgers in 2025. One playoff series, a ridiculously small sample size compared to nearly 300 games, doesn’t change that.

Their rotation though, will be missing Brandon Woodruff for the remainder of the season. Breakout starter Kyle Harrison is on the injured list, though is expected to rejoin the rotation soon. It’s a very good staff already, though not without some question marks. So who better to pair with the virtually unhittable Jacob Misiorowski in a playoff series than Tarik Skubal? A postseason rotation with Misiorowski, Skubal, Harrison, and another breakout, Logan Henderson, would be the best in baseball. Yes, even better than the Dodgers, particularly if Shohei Ohtani is unable to return to pitching thanks to his nagging knee injury.

Milwaukee also has a top two or three farm system in the league. They have the consensus number one overall prospect in Jesus Made. They are unlikely to be willing to sign Skubal in the offseason, making this their only opportunity to acquire him in a season where they already know they have an elite roster. If any team was set up to make a deal, considering his reasonable remaining salary, it was Milwaukee.

There’s just one problem. Their ownership does not care about winning.

Well, to be fair, they care, so long as it doesn’t interfere even slightly with the ability to rake in massive profits. Yes, if they gave up a top 30 overall prospect and two others, they might lose the surplus value calculation down the road. But if they have Tarik Skubal, they might win their first World Series…ever. Or even reach their first World Series since 1982.

Yes, Milwaukee needs prospects because they spend less money. But they’re the best in baseball at creating them from the draft and international signings. Go for it, even just once, and see if you make history and give your fans a lifelong memory. You’ll replace that prospect anyway. And again, flags fly literally forever.

But no, because down the road you might have surplus value from that prospect. Even though, of course, there are tens of millions of dollars in extra revenue available literally right now if you reach the World Series or win one.

Therein lies the problem, however. Most owners don’t think, "I’m going to maximize my chances of winning a World Series while I know my team is good." They think, "I’m going to maximize my future cost savings in excess prospect value." Or, more directly, "in 2031, there’s a 15% chance that this player produces $6 million worth of production while we’re only paying him $3 million, so we can’t possibly trade him to increase our chances of winning this season, even though we already know we’re extremely good right now and don’t know what our team will look like in 2031". Want to know what’s "ruining baseball?" That mindset right there.

The Dodgers don’t think like that, even though they’ve won two consecutive titles. Yes, partially because they have more money. But it’s not just that. It’s because they want to win, above all. How do we know? Because they spend a higher percentage of their revenue on payroll than almost anyone. They could easily, say, rake in their billions from ticket sales, television deals, advertising and merchandise, then simply…pocket it. They don’t have to spend $400 million on players to be popular in the massive, baseball-obsessed LA market, they choose to. Ownership wants to win, an apparent novelty in competitive sports, so they sacrifice hundreds of millions of dollars a year in increased profitability to boost their odds of doing so. They still turn a profit, to be sure, but just imagine how much more profit they’d make if they didn’t sign expensive players. That's exactly what the Brewers, Rays, Pirates, Marlins, Nationals, and on and on and on would do.

Milwaukee could have traded for Skubal, sold out every game he pitched the rest of the season, meaningfully increased their World Series odds, and still had a top three farm system. They cheaped out, as they always do, hoping that they get there anyway…and still enjoy the all-important one true beautiful purpose of baseball: saving a little bit of money.

LA, meanwhile, said, this is a luxury that moves our current World Series odds from 25% to 25.5%, even if we sacrifice years of controllable talent and more profitability, and did it anyway. The Brewers might have increased their odds from 10% to 15%, and said no.

Obviously when it comes to free agency, only a handful of teams operate on a semi-level playing field at the top of the market. Along with the Dodgers, the Mets, Yankees, Giants, Cubs, Red Sox, Phillies, Rangers, Angels, and Astros all play in huge markets and can afford to spend big money on free agents if they so choose. But even LA's spending doesn't always work. Kyle Tucker received a gigantic contract this offseason and has been a below average hitter this year. Edwin Diaz, their other big acquisition, has missed most of the season with an arm injury and has a 9.00 ERA in eight innings. The Mets, of course, have a payroll close to the Dodgers, and are one of the worst teams in baseball.

Milwaukee’s not going to compete with the Dodgers to sign Skubal as a free agent. The point though, is that they could compete with the Dodgers on a level playing field to trade for him right now. When they already know their team is good and in position to earn a first round bye. They chose not to.

The Cubs, who play in one of the three largest markets, have a massive national fan base, sell out game after game, and are in position to play either the Brewers or Dodgers in the NLDS. They need pitching, with Cade Horton out and some shaky back-end rotation options. Shota Imanaga, Tarik Skubal, and their elite offense though, would make them extremely dangerous in a short series. Not to mention meaningfully increase their chances of winning a three-game wild card series against Philadelphia.

Instead? They sat on the sidelines and watched the Dodgers swoop in.

Again, none of this is to say that the Dodgers don’t have immense financial advantages. They absolutely do. This trade wasn’t about those advantages though. It was about LA’s front office and ownership group putting winning first. If the rest of the league cared about optimizing their chances of winning a championship instead of crying poor and pouting over giving up projected excess value, fans would have much less to complain about. A salary cap won’t fix cheap ownership, because the Brewers, Marlins, Pirates and so on will always spend the bare minimum. Whatever the floor is, those teams will spend one dollar more than that floor. Whatever the top end is, the Dodgers will spend at the top. Free agents would still choose LA, even if the financial offers are equal, because their owners will still do everything they can to win more games. While those other teams put profitability and buying that third yacht first.

But maybe that’s the whole point anyway. Let uninformed fans complain and hope it leads to the ultimate and most cherished goal in the competitive sport they run: saving money.

item.title: Taylor Fritz got all hot and bothered talking about Sydney Sweeney while golfing
item.description: Taylor Fritz names Sydney Sweeney as his celebrity crush during a golf outing with David Dobrik and Josh Richards, admitting she got him all tee'd up.
item.content:encoded:

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

KAI TRUMP REVEALS NEW CELEBRITY CRUSH AFTER DITCHING 'OUTER BANKS' STAR DREW STARKEY

item.title: Trump targets Biden-era billion-dollar Smithsonian budgets amid anti-'woke' push
item.description: Trump's budget proposal cuts Smithsonian funding below $1 billion for the first time since 2020 as a 162-page White House report targets woke ideology.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump's effort to remake the Smithsonian is reaching the institution's bottom line, with the administration proposing its smallest budget request in years while pushing to eliminate what it calls "woke" ideology from federally funded museums and programs.

A Fox News Digital analysis of Smithsonian budget requests found the institution submitted steadily larger funding requests during the Biden administration, with annual requests rising from $1.11 billion in fiscal year 2021 to a record $1.24 billion in fiscal year 2024.

The fiscal year 2025 request also exceeded $1 billion before the Trump administration proposed reducing the institution's request below that threshold in its fiscal year 2026 and 2027 budgets—the first time since fiscal year 2020 that the Smithsonian's annual request has fallen below $1 billion.

The proposed funding reduction comes as the White House expands one of its most ambitious efforts to reshape a federally funded cultural institution, arguing the Smithsonian has promoted ideological narratives at odds with its mission and directing it to change its exhibits, programming, leadership and spending priorities.

FORMER DEMOCRATIC STAFFERS, DEI LEADERS SHAPE SMITHSONIAN LEADERSHIP AMID POLITICAL FIRESTORM

The White House's effort to root out what it calls "woke" ideology at the Smithsonian has grown into one of the most extensive reviews of the institution in decades.

Over the past 16 months, the administration has examined museum exhibits, educational programming, internal records and leadership statements, issued multiple document requests, interviewed curators and conducted on-site museum walkthroughs.

That review culminated in a 162-page White House report recommending sweeping reforms and a new round of executive actions aimed at implementing those recommendations.

The administration has ordered the Smithsonian to promote what it describes as a more accurate portrayal of American history while scrutinizing exhibits, programming and leadership across the museum complex.

INSIDE THE BEHEMOTH SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM NETWORK DRAWING FIRE FROM THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

The Smithsonian oversees 21 museums, the National Zoo and nearly 157 million objects and specimens while receiving more than $1 billion annually in federal funding, in addition to private donations and other trust revenue.

The taxpayer-supported institution has become the latest battleground in a broader national debate over patriotism, historical interpretation and the role of federally funded cultural institutions in shaping how Americans understand the nation's past.

TRUMP ORDERS SIGNS OUTSIDE SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM AMID ROW OVER ITS DEPICTION OF AMERICAN HISTORY

Whether Congress adopts the administration's proposed funding levels remains to be seen.

But alongside executive orders, museum reviews and a sweeping White House report, the budget proposal signals that the administration intends to use both policy and federal funding to reshape one of the nation's largest cultural institutions.

The Smithsonian Institute did not immediately respond to Fox New Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers credits wife for family reunion after more than a decade of estrangement
item.description: Aaron Rodgers credited his wife Brittani for helping him reconcile with his estranged parents and brother after more than a decade of family separation.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Rodgers’ wife was a key piece in the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback reconciling with his family after over a decade without having a connection.

During an interview with NFL Network’s Kyle Brandt, Rodgers shared some details about the pictures that went viral with his estranged parents and brother, as he reunited with them for "another bonding week" last month.

Rodgers shared photos on Instagram of himself with his father, Ed Rodgers, and his mother, Darla Rodgers, and brother Luke Rodgers.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

He told Brandt that his wife, Brittani, deserves "a lot of credit" for the reunion taking place.

"I’m happy to be reunited and that part of my life is a really beautiful addition and I got to give my wife a lot of credit – not that she was pushing me, because she never was, but just the way that she loves and supports me," Rodgers explained.

"Having her by my side during this process has been really special, and I miss those relationships. And there’s reasons for it that don’t need to be talked about, but I’m thankful that that’s come all the way back around."

AARON RODGERS RECONCILING WITH HIS PARENTS AFTER NEARLY A DOZEN YEARS OF ESTRANGEMENT

The bonding week also included Luke’s children, daughter Evie and son Jack.

Rodgers was candid about being "very closed off about that part of my life," and he fully intends to "keep it that way."

"But there’s been a narrative that has gone on for too long that I wanted to kind of shut down," he said. "And it’s been really beautiful to reconnect with them – all of them.

"I got to spend a long weekend recently – [where] those pictures are from. – in Nashville with my parents and my brother and his sweet wife and their incredible two kids. So, I got to be an uncle, so it’s really special."

It’s unknown if Aaron has been in contact with his other brother, Jordan Rodgers, who became widely known for revealing the family issues with the four-time NFL MVP.

Jordan appeared on ABC’s "The Bachelorette," where he won and remains married to JoJo Fletcher, and he revealed that, "Me and Aaron don’t really have that much of a relationship."

"It’s kind of the way he’s chosen to do life," Jordan added.

In 2023, though, Aaron contacted his father for the first time in almost nine years during a Lake Tahoe golf event. Then, when he was inducted into the Pleasant Valley High School Hall of Fame, he invited his parents and thanked them for their support over the years.

As for Brittani, she remains a mystery in terms of appearance. Aaron was spotted with a wedding ring at his first Steelers training camp last year, where he revealed they got married in June 2025 "a couple months" prior.

"There’s been a lot of conversation about it outside of my own conversations for so many years," Rodgers said. "You know, a big part of it was getting married and having those conversations with my wife that allowed me to kind of open up to the possibility of coming together — it’s been a couple-year process now, the conversations with [my family]."

Brittani also played a role in Rodgers playing one last season with the Steelers. He recently doubled down at training camp, saying that new head coach Mike McCarthy was a main reason he returned, but also that conversations with Brittani led to one final year.

And yes, this is it after 22 seasons in the league.

Rodgers is hoping his last ride includes another run with McCarthy at the helm. Last season under head coach Mike Tomlin, Rodgers reached the playoffs after throwing for 3,322 yards and 24 touchdowns. But Pittsburgh fell to the Houston Texans in the wild-card round at their home, Acrisure Stadium.

item.title: Hero sheepdog becomes unlikely rescue partner after unexpected move aids first responders
item.description: Drone video captures a sheepdog herding goats away from an emergency helicopter landing zone in Laguna Beach, earning praise as an honorary responder.
item.content:encoded:
A Southern California sheepdog is being hailed as an honorary first responder after police drone video captured the hardworking pup helping clear the way for an emergency helicopter.

The Laguna Beach Police Department shared drone video Friday showing officers and firefighters responding to an emergency in the city's foothills as crews prepared a landing zone for a helicopter.

As crews worked on the ground, a hardworking white sheepdog sprang into action, herding a nearby group of goats away from the landing area and helping keep the helicopter's path clear.

Drone video released by the department shows the dog weaving behind the herd as dozens of goats move up the hillside and away from the helicopter's approach.

FBI, ATLANTA POLICE TARGET UNAUTHORIZED DRONES FLYING NEAR WORLD CUP VENUES

At one point, the camera zooms in on the pup happily trotting across the hillside with its tail wagging after completing its impromptu mission.

"The sheepdog stepped up and helped guide a group of goats out of the way so the units could work," the Laguna Beach Police Department wrote in a social media post. "That's a good boy."

Officials have not publicly released details about the emergency response or what prompted the helicopter deployment.

CRUISE PASSENGER HAILED AS HERO AFTER JUMPING INTO WATER TO SAVE 84-YEAR-OLD MAN

The feel-good video quickly won over social media, where viewers crowned the four-legged helper "Sgt. Sheepdog" and praised the pup for calmly guiding the herd of goats out of the way.

"Sgt. Sheepdog 🫡," one commenter wrote.

"Hero," another added.

DOG SAVED FROM ISIS BY ARMY VETERAN 'KIDNAPPED' FROM FAMILY YARD BY LOCAL AUTHORITIES

item.title: Ms Rachel claims 'no one needs a billion dollars,' endorses Democratic progressives Abdul El-Sayed, Cori Bush
item.description: Ms. Rachel endorsed Cori Bush, Abdul El-Sayed and 10 other progressive candidates, telling her 5 million followers she backs those who protect kids.
item.content:encoded:
Popular children's YouTube educator Ms. Rachel backed a dozen progressive Democratic candidates on Friday, including former Rep. Cori Bush, D-Mo., and Michigan U.S. Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed, using her audience of more than 5 million followers to promote candidates she believes care about children.

"I think all kids and people should have medical care. I don’t think anyone needs a billion dollars ever, I think all kids should be safe from violence," Rachel Accurso said in a post on Instagram.

Accurso's slate covered House and Senate contests in eight states. It also included Vermont Rep. Becca Balint, Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon and former Tennessee state Rep. Justin Pearson.

YOUTUBE STAR MS RACHEL GIVES FUNDS TO DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL ABDUL EL-SAYED

"These are the folks I believe care about all kids," Accurso said.

Bush, who is seeking to reclaim her former St. Louis-area seat from Rep. Wesley Bell in Tuesday’s Democratic primary, is a Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) member. In early July, Bush said in a post on X that she was proud to be re-endorsed by the DSA.

"Together, we’ll work to abolish ICE, deliver Medicare for all, end wars overseas, and achieve true economic justice," Bush said.

EX-'SQUAD' MEMBER FIGHTS FOR COMEBACK AS SOCIALIST WING RAMPS UP WAR ON DEM ESTABLISHMENT

El-Sayed rejected the socialist label during a Tuesday interview with MS NOW host Jen Psaki despite him receiving endorsements from Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., El-Sayed spoke at six DSA events between 2017 and 2020.

"I’m simply not a socialist... I've studied a lot of the solutions that I fight for," El-Sayed said to Psaki. "Things like ‘Medicare-for-all,’ things like rethinking the way that our financial system implies that corporate CEOs are more interested in a quarterly bottom line than they are in the long-term sustainability of their business."

El-Sayed’s campaign platform calls for "Medicare-for-all," taxing billionaire wealth and banning corporate money in politics.

A federal filing also listed a $3,000 payment from Accurso to his campaign ahead of Tuesday’s Michigan primary against Rep. Haley Stevens. The filing did not specify whether the payment was a contribution or a loan.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Accurso also connected her endorsements to the influx of what she described as outside money in Democratic primaries.

"I think politicians shouldn’t attack each other and I don’t think big groups should be able to use millions to attack candidates," Accurso said.

The National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) previously criticized Accurso's financial support for El-Sayed, whose platform calls for an arms embargo against Israel.

NRSC spokeswoman Samantha Cantrell addressed the two in a statement to the New York Post in July.

"Abdul El-Sayed and Ms. Rachel are one and the same, forcing their socialist, they/them, anti-America agenda on our children," Cantrell said.

Accurso has increasingly used her platform, which includes a YouTube channel with more than 20 million subscribers, for political advocacy.

In June, Accurso visited Delaney Hall, an immigration detention facility in Newark, New Jersey, and traveled to Washington to urge Congress to end family detention and separation.

Accurso said on Wednesday that she is involved with politics because she cares "so much about kids and families everywhere," and said she could not watch them suffer and "not stand with them" in an Instagram post where she simultaneously endorsed El-Sayed.

Fox News Digital reached out to Accurso, Bush, the DSA and El-Sayed for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.
